recognize_zh: 前臂軸切 MRI 中，皮下有一個新月形、訊號增強的軟組織腫塊，貼附於一側皮膚，位於筋膜外，下方肌肉與骨頭未受侵犯，符合 BPDCN 常見的皮膚與皮下腫塊表現。
features: Axial MRI of the forearm, likely contrast-enhanced fat-suppressed sequence
Crescentic, hyperintense, enhancing subcutaneous soft-tissue mass along one side of the forearm
Lesion is superficial to the muscular fascia, with preserved fat planes to underlying muscle
Radius and ulna show normal cortical and marrow signal
Imaging features are non-specific and do not establish lineage
describe_en: Axial MRI of the right forearm demonstrates a crescentic, hyperintense, enhancing soft-tissue lesion within the subcutaneous tissue along one aspect of the forearm, measuring approximately 42 mm as reported. The lesion is superficial to the deep fascia, and the underlying muscles, radius and ulna appear uninvolved. These imaging features are non-specific but are compatible with a cutaneous/subcutaneous hematolymphoid infiltrate, consistent with the clinically and histologically documented blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm.

ddx.vs: MRI cannot separate hematolymphoid tumors; biopsy with immunohistochemistry is required.
Infection shows ill-defined edema along septa and possible rim-enhancing fluid collection rather than a discrete solid enhancing mass.
Sarcomas are typically deep, heterogeneous and may cross fascial planes, whereas this lesion is superficial and homogeneous.
